cards.text: Twelve spies just came back from forty days in Canaan, and ten of them gave a bad report: strong people, big walls, giants. Friend, they came back sounding like they watched a monster movie with the lights off. Now the whole congregation cries out, and that night the people weep.

cards.question: The crying turns into grumbling against Moses and Aaron, Israel's leaders. What does the whole congregation say they wish had happened?

answers.text: That they had died in Egypt
That they had stayed at Mount Sinai
That they had picked different spies

cards.question: The people say the LORD is bringing them into this land to fall by the sword.

cards.text: Then they ask if it wouldn't be better to just go back to Egypt. Friend, that's me knocking on the junk drawer from the OUTSIDE, asking to be let back IN.

cards.question: So the people say to one another: let's appoint a new ___ and head back to Egypt.

cards.text: Moses and Aaron fall facedown before the whole assembly. Then two of the spies, Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, tear their clothes.

cards.question: Joshua and Caleb walked that land too. They tell the whole congregation it is an exceedingly ___ land.
Joshua and Caleb say that if the LORD delights in Israel, someone will bring them into the land and give it to them. Who?

cards.text: Then they say, "Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they will be like bread for us." Ten spies saw GIANTS, and these two saw BREAD.

cards.question: Joshua and Caleb tell the people that Israel's army is strong enough to win on its own.
That's the pep talk from Joshua and Caleb. How does the whole congregation respond to them?

answers.text: They ask to see the fruit

cards.text: And right then, the glory of the LORD appears to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting. I bet you could hear a sprinkle drop.

cards.question: The LORD asks Moses how long this people will refuse to ___ in Him, despite all the signs He has performed among them.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He will strike them with a plague and destroy them, and make Moses into a nation greater and mightier than they are. Plenty of folks would jump at that, so watch what Moses does.

cards.question: Moses answers the LORD. Who does Moses say will hear about it, since God brought this people out from among them?
Moses warns the LORD that the nations will say He was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to give them.

cards.text: So Moses prays, quoting what the LORD declared: "The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion, forgiving iniquity and transgression." He quotes the other half too: the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished.

cards.question: Then Moses asks the LORD to ___ the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of His loving devotion.
The LORD tells Moses He has pardoned the people as Moses requested.

cards.text: Pardoned, friend. But then the LORD makes an oath, as surely as He lives and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD.

cards.question: These men saw God's glory and His signs in Egypt and the wilderness, and still tested Him ten times. What does the LORD say about them?

answers.text: None of them will see the land
They will lead the way in

cards.question: But the LORD singles out one man by name: My servant ___ has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly.

cards.text: The LORD says He will bring Caleb into the land he entered, and his descendants will inherit it. Then He gives directions for tomorrow, since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel to turn back tomorrow and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.

cards.text: Then the LORD says to Moses and Aaron, "How long will this wicked congregation grumble against Me?" He has heard the complaints the Israelites are making against Him. ALL of them.

cards.question: Earlier the people cried, "if only we had died in this wilderness!" So what does the LORD say He will do to them?

answers.text: Exactly what He heard them say
Whatever Moses asks Him to do
Send them all back to Egypt

cards.question: The LORD says only the spies who gave the bad report will fall in the wilderness.

cards.text: It's everyone twenty years of age or older who was counted in the census. None of them will enter the land, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

cards.question: So who does the LORD say He will bring into the land the people rejected?

cards.text: The children they said would become plunder will enjoy the land, but first they'll be shepherds in the wilderness. They'll suffer for their parents' unfaithfulness until the last of those bodies lies in the wilderness.

cards.question: For the forty ___ the spies explored the land, the people will bear their guilt forty ___.

cards.text: The LORD has spoken, and it happens. The men who brought out the bad report about the land are struck down by a plague before the LORD.

cards.question: Of the men who went to spy out the land, only Joshua and Caleb remain alive.
Moses passes all this on, and the people mourn bitterly. Early the next morning they head up toward the ridge of the hill country. What are they trying to do now?

answers.text: Go to the place the LORD promised
Find a road back to Egypt
Bury the men from the plague

cards.text: They even admit, "We have indeed sinned." But Moses says, "Why are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? This will not succeed!"

cards.question: Moses tells the people not to go up. Why does he say their enemies will strike them down?

answers.text: The LORD is not among them
Their army is far too small

cards.text: Moses warns that the Amalekites and Canaanites will face them there, and they will fall by the sword. They dare to go up anyway, and friend, that's me stamping away with NO dough on the counter.

cards.question: When the people go up to the ridge, Moses and the ark of the covenant of the LORD go with them.
The Amalekites and Canaanites come down from the hill country, attack Israel, and rout them all the way to ___.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 16 quotes "We have indeed sinned.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from Numbers 13: twelve spies, forty days in Canaan, ten giving a bad report, strong people, big walls and giants. The card cites only Numbers 14:1, so these outside facts carry no reference. Also, Numbers 13 says 'great in stature' and 'Nephilim', not 'giants'.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'Ten spies saw GIANTS' states a fact from Numbers 13 with no reference. The card cites only Numbers 14:9. Numbers 13:32-33 says 'great in stature' and 'Nephilim', not 'giants'.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The first blank's answer, 'days', was already given in stop 1 card 1: 'Twelve spies just came back from forty days in Canaan.' The baker gets that blank for free.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'ALL of them' adds to Numbers 14:27, which says only 'I have heard the complaints that the Israelites are making against Me.' It isn't a joke, so it stretches the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Wrong answer 'The Levites' is arguable. The Levites were not counted in the census (Num 1:47-49), so a baker who knows that could argue they were not under the judgment of 14:29 and did enter the land.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This is the first time the Amalekites and Canaanites appear, and the card doesn't say who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Stop 2's story cards are almost all plain retelling. Only card 18 carries a real laugh, and cards 1, 4, 9, 11 and 13 read like a neutral summary with little of Papa Dorin's voice. Some moments could hold a laugh without muddying a fact, like the people suddenly deciding to march up the morning after refusing (14:40).

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
